CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep nonparametric methods changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Keep nonparametric methods outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. Before starting nonparametric methods work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. When nonparametric methods decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen nonparametric methods approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. When multiple nonparametric methods strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. Check that nonparametric methods terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to nonparametric methods (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. Prefer the simplest nonparametric methods approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. Validate nonparametric methods outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. Document any non-obvious nonparametric methods decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic nonparametric methods advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated nonparametric methods concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting nonparametric methods assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about nonparametric methods over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
